narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 72.6% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a risk estimate, not a certainty, but it means the model judged failure more likely than passing, so your application was rejected.

The strongest factor was your LSAT score of 23, which is well below the average of about 37 among accepted students; this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was very close to the accepted-student average of 3.23, so it provided a small counterweight toward passing. Your first-year class rank was in the third decile, compared with an average around the sixth decile among accepted students, and this also pushed the prediction toward failure, though less strongly than the LSAT. Your gender and race were not used to make the prediction.

To strengthen a future application, focus first on substantially improving your LSAT performance through structured preparation and retesting. Also seek admissions feedback, consider strengthening your academic record if possible, and speak with a pre-law advisor about whether postponing and reapplying with stronger credentials would improve your chances.
